authority.legal_name: TransLink (South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority)
authority.home_waters_label: Burrard Inlet and the lower Fraser

mandate.summary: TransLink is Metro Vancouver's regional transportation authority, running the integrated bus, SkyTrain and SeaBus network — including the SeaBus passenger ferry across Burrard Inlet between downtown Vancouver and North Vancouver.
current_priorities: Integrating water transport into the Compass-card network
Decarbonizing the fleet under the Climate Action Strategy
Relieving the bridges and Highway 1 across the region

policy_targets.net_zero_year: 2050 (Metro Vancouver carbon neutral; TransLink Climate Action Strategy)
policy_targets.vision: TransLink Climate Action Strategy / Metro Vancouver Climate 2050
policy_targets.decarb_note: TransLink targets a zero-emission fleet under its Climate Action Strategy, and the SeaBus runs a single high-demand crossing — but the big SeaBus hulls can't economically open the other cross-inlet links the region needs.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission foiling layer that lets TransLink add the cross-inlet and up-inlet lines the big SeaBus hulls can't run economically — fast, quiet crossings that relieve the bridges, on the same integrated network.

precedent.headline: Public passenger ferries are core transport infrastructure here — the SeaBus is one of the busiest in North America.
precedent.network: TransLink's SeaBus carries millions of passengers a year across Burrard Inlet between Waterfront and Lonsdale Quay, fully integrated into the Compass-card network alongside SkyTrain and bus.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling layer that lets TransLink add the cross-inlet and up-inlet lines the big SeaBus hulls can't run economically — fast, quiet crossings that relieve the bridges, on the same integrated network.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The live SeaBus crossing — downtown to North Vancouver across Burrard Inlet.
New fast cross-inlet line to West Vancouver's Ambleside — a crossing the big SeaBus hulls don't serve.
North-shore waterfront link between Lonsdale and Ambleside.
East-inlet line to the North Vancouver employment lands.
Up-inlet commuter line to Port Moody at the head of Burrard Inlet.
Fraser River line to New Westminster Quay.

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across Burrard Inlet and the lower Fraser. Sunshine Coast / Vancouver Island links are secondary and out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: Burrard Inlet is a major commercial port with tanker and bulk traffic — cross the shipping channel at marked points; waypoint clear of anchorages and the Second Narrows.
The Lions Gate (First Narrows) and Ironworkers Memorial (Second Narrows) bridge piers and strong tidal currents at the narrows require hand-waypointing.
The Fraser has strong currents, log booms and shifting sandbars — follow the marked navigation channel.
Up-inlet routes pass sensitive habitat — low-wake operation near the shore.
